title_en: Jobs (6/20): A Case for the Lawyer
note_en: 被 marks the passive and names the doer right after it: 他被公司无理由解雇了 "he was fired by the company for no reason." Where English needs "was" plus a past participle, Chinese leaves the verb unchanged and lets 被 do the work. The doer can also be left out: 甚至被吊销执业证 "even have their license revoked." Note that 被 often hints that something unwelcome happened to the subject.
